title: Tin Hinan
summary: Tin Hinan is the legendary ancestor of the Ahaggar Tuareg, said in one source to have lived in the 4th century. A circular stone monument at Abalessa in the Hoggar of southern Algeria, excavated in 1925 by a Franco-American mission and again in 1933, held the skeleton of a woman with gold and silver bracelets. Tuareg accounts about her and her tomb are inconsistent, and whether this is her tomb remains uncertain.

uncertainty.note: No documents date her. Let Africa Speak calls her "a legendary woman that lived in the 4th Century"; the page says there is no record of her tribe, husband, parents or cause of death. Gast (1973) reports contradictory Tuareg testimony, including an informant who said her true tomb was a different one at the base of the hill.

where.modern_name: Tomb of Tin Hinan (the Abalessa monument), Abalessa, Tamanrasset Province, Algeria (pinned to the tomb attributed to her, not to a place of her life)
where.historical_name: Abalessa in the Hoggar (Ahaggar), the Tuareg homeland in the central Sahara, in late antiquity before any named polity; the 4th-century date and the identification with Tin Hinan rest on tradition

importance.justification: Tuareg tradition treats her as an ancestress ("Mother of Us All" in the sources), and the Abalessa tomb is the physical site tied to her.
